transcript.answer: No. Otto forbids any tool from declaring a customer number, or any customer, company or account identifier, in its input schema (FR-034). `enforceNoCustomerInput` in `apps/api/src/tools/toolAuth.ts` checks every property name at any depth and throws an error when a tool declares one, so the tool is refused before it can register. A test, `apps/api/test/customerBoundary.test.ts`, walks every registered tool to confirm none do. The customer number comes from the verified login token's `customer_number` claim, which `toolAuth.ts` re-verifies on each call. The model never supplies it. For example, `get_booking_status` takes only `booking_reference`. The reason is that the TMS uses one server-held API key, so a model-supplied customer identifier would bypass the customer boundary (ADR-001).
